newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas seen with 4.4 bln Ffr 96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Paribas seen with 4.4 bln Ffr 96 profit.

text.p: French financial holding company Groupe Paribas should return to profit in 1996 after a loss of four billion francs in 1995, analysts said.

On average, 11 analysts in a Reuter survey forecast the company would show a profit of 4.38 billion francs for 1996, after losing 3.998 billion francs in 1995 due mostly to a writedown of its stake in Cie de Navigation Mixte.
At the time, Paribas owned 31 percent of Mixte. It now controls nearly all the company after a successful takeover launched in February 1996.
The predictions for 1996 profits, which add little to the company's first half profit of 4.042 billion francs, show it made only modest profits in the second half of the year, analysts said.
First-half profits were driven by capital gains, which the company was unable to duplicate later in the year, they added.

The profit will come despite a 1.23 billion franc loss at its Cie Bancaire unit. Bancaire announced the loss on February 20 and blamed it mostly on 2.48 billion francs of provisions to cover its exposure to real estate activities. In 1996, Bancaire earned 602 million francs.
Analysts were also predicting that Paribas' fortunes would probably continue to improve this year with one forecasting a profit of 5.22 billion francs in 1997.

But some said that the company's share price already reflected the positive profit outlook and that barring major developments or restructuring, the share was unlikely to rise sharply from its current levels.
At 1200 GMT, Paribas was up 2.93 percent at 394 francs, well above its twelve-month low of 248.10 francs but off its twelve-month high of 410 francs.
Other financial stocks were also higher as investors cheered improved profit expectations at French banks.
